1.why: The system verifies that the supplied reset token digest matches the recovery record stored in the user's active session object.

2.why: Reset token digests are stored on individual session records and will not validate for any other user session.

3.why: The application does not track user identities across sessions or invalidate other active sessions when a password is changed.

4.why: The Bun server requires TLS certificates and enforces HTTPS along with Strict-Transport-Security headers.

5.why: Reset codes are hashed using SHA-256 and passwords are hashed using bcrypt with a cost factor of 12.

6.why: No private user contact details are logged, stored, or exposed in any messages generated by the system.

7.why: Server-side HTML escaping is applied to dynamic values and client-side rendering relies on safe DOM textContent methods.

8.why: All navigation is restricted to internal client-side hash routing within the single-page application.

9.why: There are no email templates in the application and user inputs are never rendered into raw HTML templates.

10.why: Reset tokens and MFA security codes are explicitly written to the browser console and the visible UI logs panel.

11.why: The multi-factor authentication security code is hardcoded as a plain text string directly in the source code.

12.why: The system contains no default administrative accounts or pre-configured default credentials.

13.why: Session and IP-based rate limiting buckets throttle and block repeated failed verification requests.

14.why: The recovery endpoint returns a generic success response regardless of the contact value submitted.

15.why: Reset codes are created using 32 bytes of cryptographically secure pseudo-random base64url data.
